reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review contract, resource assessment rubric, and fresh-review framework; then read the Library resource context, full StructureDefinition report, deterministic aggregate, direct SearchParameter behavior finding, shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context, R4/R6 Library StructureDefinition evidence for the material paths, and the R4 maturity map. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only because the assigned resource is `Library`.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 Library is trial-use/FMM 2, so it does not carry normative or high-FMM stability pressure. That lowers the presumption against change, but it does not erase the practical importance of Library metadata in clinical decision support, package resolution, canonical artifact discovery, and production-use gating.

overall.oneLineConclusion: Library keeps its identity and remains structurally loadable from R4, but targeted semantic and conformance-identity changes still deserve per-change compatibility preservation.

reasoning.thesisMd: R6 does not redesign Library as a resource. There are no local removed elements, no required additions, no cardinality tightening, no reference-target removals, and no hard old-valid/new-invalid instance breaks in the Library structure report. The real migration shape is a set of targeted metadata semantics, warning constraints, terminology canonical changes, generated-model/rendering adjustments, and search-conformance identity changes.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: Most R4 Library instances can be structurally carried into R6. `usage` changes from `string` to `markdown` but remains the same JSON string wire shape. `versionAlgorithm[x]` and `copyrightLabel` are optional R6-only additions. `url`, `name`, and `relatedArtifact` add or tighten warning-level constraints rather than base validity. The paths that require policy attention are mainly `jurisdiction`, whose meaning shifts from intended-use jurisdiction toward maintaining-authority jurisdiction, `experimental`, whose lifecycle meaning becomes stronger across versions, `type`, whose binding canonical moves, and the canonical SearchParameter definitions consolidated under CanonicalResource/MetadataResource.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because a resource-wide migration program is not already unavoidable, each avoidable local break still has normal leverage. Even where local migration chores are manageable, preserving old semantic expectations, canonical aliases, or transition metadata would reduce risk without having to preserve an obsolete Library model. The direct SearchParameter change is broad conformance churn, not a Library instance migration, so it reinforces per-change preservation rather than changing the resource-level posture to migration-dominates.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest low-cost alternatives are standards-level compatibility devices: retain or explicitly alias the old `Library.type` value set canonical while moving stewardship to THO; publish deprecated aliases for consolidated canonical SearchParameter URLs; avoid silently reinterpreting `Library.jurisdiction` by preserving the R4 intended-use meaning or introducing a distinct maintainer-jurisdiction signal; and avoid overloading `experimental` with a permanent all-versions lifecycle meaning without a separate governance signal or clear transition rule. Warning-level constraints on `url`, `name`, and `relatedArtifact` are already comparatively compatibility-preserving and mostly become implementation guidance.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The one direct behavior finding for Library is SearchParameter canonical consolidation. Query codes generally remain available, but clients, CapabilityStatement comparison tools, generated clients, and registries that key on exact SearchParameter canonical URLs can conclude support disappeared. This is standards-review-worthy because alias/deprecation support appears plausible. The 11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings, including Resource-level operation removals and special search parameter metadata changes, are important platform context but were not scored as Library-specific migration drivers.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate's headline result: major migration already unavoidable = `No`, migration shape = `mostly-stable-with-local-breaks`, and compatibility posture = `preserve-compatibility-per-change`. The independent review gives slightly more emphasis to the business meaning of Library metadata (`jurisdiction`, `experimental`, search conformance identity), but those issues are still targeted enough that they do not make a resource-level migration program dominate.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the structural shape and selected R4/R6 element evidence. The main residual uncertainty is terminology and prevalence: external THO expansions and real-world dependence on exact Library SearchParameter/value set canonical URLs were not exhaustively measured from the local package.

findingConsiderations.title: Library.jurisdiction meaning changes from intended-use jurisdiction to maintaining-authority jurisdiction
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the clearest Library-specific semantic break. R4 data can remain structurally valid but be read with a different meaning in R6, affecting artifact discovery, regulatory filtering, and applicability decisions. It does not force a broad model migration, but it is worth preserving or explicitly transitioning.

findingConsiderations.title: Library.experimental semantics are strengthened to mean no version will ever be for real use
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The boolean wire shape is unchanged, but the lifecycle meaning becomes stronger and can disrupt publishers that used `experimental=true` for pre-production versions under a canonical later used for production. This is local and semantic, not a structural remodel, but it deserves standards attention.

findingConsiderations.title: Library.type extensible binding canonical moves to terminology.hl7.org
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `Library.type` remains required and structurally unchanged, but binding-aware tooling may key on the old canonical. A deprecated alias or explicit canonical transition could preserve compatibility at low cost while still moving stewardship.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 consolidates many per-resource canonical SearchParameter URLs into multi-base CanonicalResource and MetadataResource definitions
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This directly affects Library conformance metadata even though query codes generally survive. Exact canonical matching in CapabilityStatements, generated clients, or search registries can break. It is avoidable or reducible with aliases, but it does not make Library instance migration unavoidable.

findingConsiderations.title: Library.usage changes primitive type from string to markdown
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This can affect generated APIs and rendering/sanitization behavior, but the JSON value remains a string and ordinary R4 instances should not become invalid. It is a local migration chore once R6's computable markdown goal is accepted.

findingConsiderations.title: Library.subject[x] binding changes from subject-type/resource-types to participant-resource-types/fhir-types
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The element shape and Group reference target remain stable and the binding remains extensible, so this is warning-level terminology pressure rather than a hard instance break. It matters for terminology-aware tooling but is not a resource-level migration driver.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds warning that dependency/component relatedArtifacts should reference a resource
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The warning can affect package and dependency-resolution workflows for executable Libraries, but it is not an error-level base constraint. It is best treated as implementation migration guidance rather than evidence of a major Library remodel.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds warning constraint that Library.url should not contain pipe, hash, or space
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a warning-level canonical hygiene constraint with unchanged element type and cardinality. It may require warning policy tuning, but it is already a compatibility-conscious form of the rule.

findingConsiderations.title: Library.name machine-identifier warning is tightened and renamed from lib-0 to cnl-0
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The main effects are warning-key churn and a narrow one-character-name edge case. It does not affect base validity and does not influence the resource-level migration conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds Library.versionAlgorithm[x] for version comparison
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This optional addition creates R6-to-R4 round-trip loss when populated, but it does not invalidate or reinterpret R4 Library instances during R4-to-R6 migration.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds Library.copyrightLabel as a short copyright display string
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is an optional metadata convenience element. It may need an extension or copy policy for R6-to-R4 export, but it is not an R4-to-R6 compatibility pressure.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This can be a high-impact platform behavior change for Resource-level APIs, but it is shared context rather than a Library-specific structure or behavior finding. It should not be counted as evidence that Library itself requires a resource-level migration program.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource/DomainResource search metadata issue may affect generic clients, but it is not specific to Library and remains outside the resource-level score.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit the `Library.jurisdiction` and `Library.experimental` semantic changes with explicit transition guidance or separate signals so R4 metadata is not silently reinterpreted in R6.
Provide alias/deprecation handling for compatibility-sensitive canonical identities: the old `Library.type` value set URL and Library-related per-resource SearchParameter canonical URLs.

Migration guidance for implementers should call out targeted Library metadata audits: `jurisdiction` to `useContext` policy, `experimental` version history, warning-level `relatedArtifact` dependency checks, markdown rendering for `usage`, and matching SearchParameters by base/code/type rather than canonical URL alone.
Document R6-to-R4 export policy for optional R6-only fields such as `versionAlgorithm[x]` and `copyrightLabel`; these are round-trip concerns, not reasons to block the R6 additions.

caveats: External terminology expansions were not fully resolved from the local package, so terminology impact is judged from binding metadata and reported evidence.
The review treats shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings as context only, consistent with the resource-review contract.
The conclusion is about R4-to-R6 Library compatibility; R6-to-R4 round-trip losses are noted only where they affect migration posture.
